assessment.report:
# Repair-loop guard documentation readiness

The Lead reviewed the latest user-approved design and existing execution, routing, TDD, documentation and handoff boundaries. Ordinary repair 2/3 and explicit debug 3/6 have distinct counters; consecutive unproductive diagnosis can pause earlier. Human reports need causal hypotheses with evidence/confidence, precise inputs and bounded next steps. Issue identity follows acceptance behavior/conditions/deviation, not the chosen implementation. Long healthy operations use evidence-based checkpoints without universal time limits.

The existing source layout is adequate. One canonical shared reference will own policy; Skills link to it, templates expose minimal history and pause state, and the active stage packet owns verification/manual evidence. Public English/Chinese release information stays paired; 0.9.4 is a patch extension, not a stable promotion. No PRD or OpenSpec authority is active for this bounded task. No new application Blueprint or source restructuring is warranted.

Only the selected scope was assessed. Unrelated inventoried documents and previous task results are preserved, not re-certified. The new reference is tracked as absent before implementation; creation or edits invalidate this review and require a fresh close assessment. The Tester packet was prepared and validated before writer GO. Native/doc/isolated package/fake-home checks and independent review remain required. Future Agent compliance and user acceptance are manual pending.

Actual selected writer is team-docs-maintainer at /root/repair_guard_writer_v2; reused Tester is /root/concurrency_tester with prior selection evidence. Unreported runtime identity/model remains unknown. No local installation, external service, Git write, unsafe experiment or automatic runtime enforcement is authorized.
